lead: Rheinmetall / RHM.DE — Europe is finally spending
smaller: Tesla / TSLA — the worst month since 2022
AST SpaceMobile / ASTS — the Starlink rival with a European partner
why_lead: Tesla is replaced as lead. It has been the subject of the last two editions (3 March smaller trade 'is $700 still on the table?' and 4 March smaller trade 'the top pick is back'), and the draft lead repeated the 4 March catalysts (Morgan Stanley's top pick, Musk's tenfold profit claim, the chairwoman's $33 million sale, Berkshire passing Tesla, the Korean leveraged-ETF losses), which are not changed stories. Tesla returns only as a smaller trade on the new evidence: the 4 March China-made sales report and CNBC's worst-month-since-2022 headline. Rheinmetall meets all three lead tests on today's evidence: a surge (1,122 euros, up 47.98 percent over 20 sessions and 17.76 percent over five), retail-press attention in this feed (Bankier.pl, This is Money, Investing.com Polska), and a simple policy story (the EU's 800 billion euro plan and Europe's $840 billion plan, reported 3 and 4 March). No earlier edition led or covered Rheinmetall.
why_smaller: Tesla returns as a smaller trade on a changed story: the 4 March China-made sales report (lowest since August 2022) and CNBC's worst-month-since-2022 headline are new since the 4 March smaller trade, and the arson report is new since the 3 March one. The Morgan Stanley and Musk catalysts are dropped.

AST SpaceMobile is the satellite trade, not a Tesla or defence trade: the Vodafone European agreement reported on 3 March and the 4 March MWC coverage are new catalysts, and the stock rose 11.67 percent in the prior session.

TSMC is the chip-deal trade in which retail stayed bullish while the price slid to a four-month low (Stocktwits, 3 March); the 4 March Taiwan confirmation that most advanced chips are excluded is the new risk, and no earlier edition covered the chip deal.
considered_not_chosen: Palantir (PLTR): an analyst call on Pentagon cuts popped the stock about 5 percent in one session [n2670], but the card shows +1.17 percent in the prior session and only +0.79 percent over 20 sessions, so there is no sustained move behind the headline.
Sandisk (SNDK): retail is excited about the relisted stock and an analyst's upside call [n5751], but the card has no 20-session return for it, so the price half of the test cannot be measured.

Nebius (NBIS): it crashed on Monday [n5747] and is down 11.11 percent over 20 sessions, but there is no dated catalyst and the attention is generic AI-infrastructure enthusiasm rather than a trade of its own.

Super Micro (SMCI): up 45.77 percent over 20 sessions after a filing that cleared the deadline [n2378]; it is a relief move on a filing, with no simple crowd thesis that would carry several days of attention.

Gold and gold miners: gold is up 2.22 percent over 20 sessions and the '$3,000' framing [n7740] has no price surge behind it, so it is too thin for a lead, and it is already covered as a materials sentiment point.

Nuclear reactor names (OKLO, SMR, NNE): deep 20-session drawdowns, with Oklo down 32.68 percent, but the headlines in this window are policy items; the fuel chain is used instead as an underowned theme.
Bitcoin miners (CIFR, IREN, RIOT, MARA): sharp 20-session drawdowns with no retail-attention headlines in this window, so there is no crowd story to write about.
Oil and OPEC+: WTI is down 6.70 percent over 20 sessions on the output hike [n7833], which is clear price evidence, but no retail-attention headline exists for crude, so it fails the attention test.
Mixue (Hong Kong IPO): the debut jumped 43 percent [n3370] and set a record for retail subscriptions, but that is a one-off listing event rather than a narrative the crowd repeats across days.

Tesla as the full lead: the draft lead repeated the 4 March catalysts (Morgan Stanley's $430 top pick [n5623], Musk's tenfold profit claim [n2637], Berkshire passing Tesla [n2616], the chairwoman's $33 million sale [n7379] and the Korean leveraged-ETF losses [n5472]). A changed price alone does not make a new essay, so Tesla returns only as a smaller trade on the 4 March sales evidence.

XRP (XRP-USD): the reserve story led on 3 March and was the 'reserve rally that faltered' smaller trade on 4 March; the Eric Trump 'win for retail' item [n1774] and the 11.67 percent five-session rebound repeat the same catalyst, with no new product, regulatory or result event.

IonQ (IONQ): the 3 March smaller trade used the 'million bucks by 2030' hook and the same $500 million at-the-market and ID Quantique facts [n5494][n5353][n5357]; the Microsoft quantum chip [n5621] is the only new element, and the 46.11 percent 20-session fall is a changed price, not a changed story.
Zero-day options / VIX: the 4 March lead; the record 0DTE headline [n5670] is already spent, and a VIX move alone does not make a new trade.
Alibaba (BABA): up 31.68 percent over 20 sessions, but the feed carries AI-capex and Jack Ma headlines [n0858][n1119] and no dated retail-attention item on the stock.
Cathie Wood and Beam Therapeutics: ARK's eight straight days of buying [n5684] is an attention item, but BEAM has no card entry, so the price half of the test cannot be measured.

NuScale (SMR) re-entry: the 4 March smaller trade already used NuScale's AI-power story; the 3 March results [n2665] predate that trade, so they are not a changed story, and the 11.52 percent one-day move has no dated catalyst in the feed.
